title: Polynomial rigidity of strong-field magnetic billiards
summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded domain whose boundary $γ$ is a smooth simple closed curve, and let $r=|B|^{-1}$ be the Larmor radius of a constant magnetic field. Assume $$ 0<r<\frac{r_0(γ)}2, $$ where $r_0(γ)$ is the maximal embedded tubular radius of $γ$. We prove that if the corresponding magnetic billiard admits a nonconstant first integral polynomial in the velocity, then $γ$ is a circle and $Ω$ is a disk. No convexity assumption is imposed. This eliminates the finite set of possible exceptional strong-field values left by the earlier polynomial nonintegrability theory. The proof…
